text:
The first recorded European landing on the Australian mainland was by the Dutch, led by Willem Janszoon, captain of the ship *Duyfken*. In February–March 1606, his crew landed on the western side of Cape York Peninsula, near the Pennefather River in modern Queensland. They were exploring the New Guinea coast and mistook the land for an extension of it. A skirmish with local Aboriginal people reportedly resulted in some crew deaths.

Earlier European contact is sometimes speculated, such as Portuguese or Spanish voyages, but nothing is firmly documented. Dirk Hartog's 1616 landing on an island off Western Australia was later, and Cook's 1770 landing at Botany Bay came much later still.
